\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{index::doc}}


\sphinxAtStartPar
PicoGL is a lightweight Python OpenGL wrapper designed for educational purposes and simple 3D graphics applications. It provides a clean, easy\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}use interface for OpenGL operations while maintaining compatibility with both modern and legacy OpenGL systems.

\sphinxhref{https://www.python.org/downloads/}{\sphinxincludegraphics{{python-badge}.png}}

\sphinxhref{https://www.opengl.org/}{\sphinxincludegraphics{{opengl-badge}.png}}

\sphinxhref{https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT}{\sphinxincludegraphics{{license-badge}.png}}


\chapter{Features}
\label{\detokenize{index:features}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}platform compatibility}: Works on Windows, macOS, and Linux

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Legacy OpenGL support}: Compatible with OpenGL 1.x, 2.x, and 3.3+

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Educational focus}: Clean, well\sphinxhyphen{}documented code for learning OpenGL

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiple backends}: Support for both modern and legacy rendering pipelines

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Comprehensive examples}: From simple cubes to complex molecular visualizations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Unit testing}: Full test coverage for all major components

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Troubleshooting}
\label{\detokenize{installation:troubleshooting}}

\subsubsection{Common Issues}
\label{\detokenize{installation:common-issues}}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{ImportError: No module named ‘OpenGL’}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install PyOpenGL: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pip install PyOpenGL PyOpenGL\sphinxhyphen{}accelerate}}

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{ImportError: No module named ‘numpy’}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install NumPy: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pip install numpy}}

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{ImportError: No module named ‘pyglm’}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install PyGLM: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pip install pyglm}}

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{OpenGL context creation failed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Update graphics drivers and ensure OpenGL is supported

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{Segmentation fault on macOS}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Run from Terminal.app or iTerm2, not from IDE

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{Black screen or no rendering}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check OpenGL support and try software rendering

\end{description}


\subsubsection{macOS Specific Issues}
\label{\detokenize{installation:macos-specific-issues}}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{“No OpenGL context” error}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Run from Terminal.app or iTerm2

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check if XQuartz is installed and running

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Try software rendering: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export MESA\_GL\_VERSION\_OVERRIDE=3.3}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{“Shader compilation failed” error}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use legacy examples instead

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check OpenGL version support

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{“Segmentation fault” error}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Run from Terminal.app

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check OpenGL drivers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Try different OpenGL settings

\end{itemize}

\end{description}


\subsubsection{Windows Specific Issues}
\label{\detokenize{installation:windows-specific-issues}}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{“Microsoft Visual C++ 14.0 is required”}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install Visual Studio Build Tools

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{Quick Start Guide}
\label{\detokenize{quickstart:quick-start-guide}}\label{\detokenize{quickstart::doc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{quickstart:understanding-the-code}}

Let’s break down what this code does:
\begin{enumerate}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Import PicoGL modules}:
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MeshData}}: Container for vertex and color data
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RenderWindow}}: Window for displaying 3D content

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Define colors}: One color per vertex

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\subsection{Key Concepts}
\label{\detokenize{quickstart:key-concepts}}

\subsubsection{MeshData}
\label{\detokenize{quickstart:meshdata}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MeshData}} is the core data structure in PicoGL. It holds all the information needed to render a 3D object:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{data} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{MeshData}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}raw}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{vertices}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{vertices}\PYG{p}{,}    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 3D positions}
    \PYG{n}{colors}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{colors}\PYG{p}{,}        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} RGB colors}
    \PYG{n}{normals}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{normals}\PYG{p}{,}      \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Surface normals (optional)}
    \PYG{n}{uvs}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{uvs}              \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Texture coordinates (optional)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{RenderWindow}
\label{\detokenize{quickstart:renderwindow}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RenderWindow}} provides the display interface. It handles:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
OpenGL context creation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Window management

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
User input (mouse, keyboard)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rendering loop

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{window} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{RenderWindow}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{width}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{800}\PYG{p}{,}           \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Window width}
    \PYG{n}{height}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{600}\PYG{p}{,}          \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Window height}
    \PYG{n}{title}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{My App}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}      \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Window title}
    \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{mesh\PYGZus{}data}       \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Mesh to display}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Interactive Controls}
\label{\detokenize{quickstart:interactive-controls}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default controls are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Mouse drag}: Rotate the view

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Mouse wheel}: Zoom in/out

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{R key}: Reset rotation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{W key}: Toggle wireframe mode

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ESC key}: Exit

\end{itemize}

\section{Legacy Examples}
\label{\detokenize{legacy_examples:legacy-examples}}\label{\detokenize{legacy_examples::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PicoGL includes comprehensive legacy examples designed to work on systems with limited OpenGL support, including older macOS systems and systems without modern shader support.


\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{legacy_examples:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The legacy examples provide multiple fallback renderers that work on systems with limited OpenGL support:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Minimal versions}: Use only PyOpenGL, maximum compatibility

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Fixed versions}: Use PicoGL with legacy rendering, medium compatibility

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Original versions}: Use modern OpenGL 3.3+, low compatibility

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Why Legacy Examples?}
\label{\detokenize{legacy_examples:why-legacy-examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modern OpenGL (3.3+) requires:
* Shader compilation support
* Vertex Array Objects (VAOs)
* Modern graphics drivers
* Specific OpenGL context requirements

\sphinxAtStartPar
Legacy examples work on:
* Older macOS systems
* Systems without shader support
* Systems with limited OpenGL drivers
* Headless environments (with proper setup)
* Educational environments with restricted OpenGL

\subsection{Performance Notes}
\label{\detokenize{legacy_examples:performance-notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Minimal Versions}:
* Fastest performance
* Uses hardware\sphinxhyphen{}optimized primitives
* Immediate mode rendering
* No shader compilation overhead

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Fixed Versions}:
* Medium performance
* Uses legacy VBOs
* Some shader compilation
* Better integration with PicoGL

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Original Versions}:
* Slowest performance
* Full shader pipeline
* Modern VAO/VBO usage
* Maximum feature set


\subsection{Choosing the Right Version}
\label{\detokenize{legacy_examples:choosing-the-right-version}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use Minimal Versions When}:
* Maximum compatibility is required
* OpenGL support is limited
* Performance is critical
* No PicoGL integration needed

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use Fixed Versions When}:
* PicoGL integration is desired
* Some OpenGL support is available
* Balance between compatibility and features
* OBJ file loading is needed

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use Original Versions When}:
* Full OpenGL 3.3+ support is available
* Maximum features are needed
* Modern shader pipeline is required
* Best visual quality is desired

\subsection{Performance Issues}
\label{\detokenize{troubleshooting:performance-issues}}

\subsubsection{Slow Rendering}
\label{\detokenize{troubleshooting:slow-rendering}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Causes}:
* Too many draw calls
* Inefficient shaders
* Large textures
* Poor buffer management

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solutions}:
* Use instanced rendering
* Optimize shaders
* Use appropriate texture sizes
* Batch similar operations

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example}:
.. code\sphinxhyphen{}block:: python
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Inefficient rendering
for obj in objects:
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
obj.render()  \# Many draw calls
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Efficient rendering
batch\_objects(objects)
render\_batch()  \# Single draw call
\end{quote}


\subsubsection{Memory Issues}
\label{\detokenize{troubleshooting:memory-issues}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Causes}:
* Large textures
* Too many buffers
* Memory leaks
* Inefficient data structures

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solutions}:
* Use appropriate texture sizes
* Clean up unused buffers
* Monitor memory usage
* Use efficient data types

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example}:
.. code\sphinxhyphen{}block:: python
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Memory leak
def create\_mesh():
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
vao = VertexArrayObject()
\# … use vao …
\# Forgot to delete vao
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Fixed
def create\_mesh():
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
vao = VertexArrayObject()
try:
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# … use vao …
\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{finally:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
vao.delete()

\end{description}
\end{quote}
\end{quote}


\subsubsection{Frame Rate Issues}
\label{\detokenize{troubleshooting:frame-rate-issues}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Causes}:
* VSync enabled
* Too many operations per frame
* Inefficient rendering
* Poor OpenGL state management

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solutions}:
* Disable VSync if needed
* Optimize rendering loop
* Use efficient rendering techniques
* Minimize state changes

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example}:
.. code\sphinxhyphen{}block:: python
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Inefficient rendering
def render():
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
glEnable(GL\_DEPTH\_TEST)
draw\_object1()
glDisable(GL\_DEPTH\_TEST)
glEnable(GL\_DEPTH\_TEST)
draw\_object2()
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Efficient rendering
def render():
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
glEnable(GL\_DEPTH\_TEST)
draw\_object1()
draw\_object2()
glDisable(GL\_DEPTH\_TEST)
\end{quote}
\end{quote}

\subsubsection{Try Legacy Examples}
\label{\detokenize{troubleshooting:try-legacy-examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If modern examples don’t work, try legacy examples:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Fixed examples (PicoGL integration)}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Update Dependencies}
\label{\detokenize{troubleshooting:update-dependencies}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Update all dependencies to latest versions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }picogl\PYG{+w}{ }numpy\PYG{+w}{ }PyOpenGL\PYG{+w}{ }PyOpenGL\PYGZhy{}accelerate\PYG{+w}{ }pyglm\PYG{+w}{ }Pillow

\label{\detokenize{troubleshooting:check-opengl-support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Verify OpenGL support on your system:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{OpenGL}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{GL}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{GL}

\subsubsection{Use Software Rendering}
\label{\detokenize{troubleshooting:use-software-rendering}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If hardware rendering fails, try software rendering:

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxstylestrong{Example}:

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create modern mesh}
\PYG{n}{mesh} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{GLMesh}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{vertices}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{vertices}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{faces}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{faces}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{colors}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{colors}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{normals}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{normals}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Upload to GPU and draw}
\PYG{n}{mesh}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{upload}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{mesh}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{draw}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsection{Data Structures}
\label{\detokenize{api/renderer:data-structures}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The renderer module uses several data structures to represent 3D mesh information:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Vertices}: 3D positions of mesh vertices
\sphinxstylestrong{Colors}: RGB color values for each vertex
\sphinxstylestrong{Normals}: Surface normal vectors for lighting
\sphinxstylestrong{UVs}: Texture coordinates for texture mapping
\sphinxstylestrong{Faces}: Triangle indices defining mesh topology

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Vertex data (N, 3) array}
\PYG{n}{vertices} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Vertex 0}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Vertex 1}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}   \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Vertex 2}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{float32}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Color data (N, 3) array}

    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Green}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}   \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Blue}

\subsection{Rendering Pipeline}
\label{\detokenize{api/renderer:rendering-pipeline}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The PicoGL rendering pipeline follows these steps:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data Preparation}: Create MeshData with vertices, colors, normals, etc.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Context Setup}: Initialize GLContext with shaders and OpenGL state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Renderer Creation}: Create appropriate renderer (ObjectRenderer, TextureRenderer, etc.)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Initialization}: Call renderer.initialize() to set up OpenGL resources

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Rendering}: Call renderer.render() to draw the mesh

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 1. Prepare data}
\PYG{n}{data} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{MeshData}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}raw}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{vertices}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{vertices}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{colors}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{colors}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 2. Setup context}
\PYG{n}{context} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{GLContext}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{context}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{create\PYGZus{}shader\PYGZus{}program}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{vertex.glsl}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{fragment.glsl}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 3. Create renderer}
\PYG{n}{renderer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{ObjectRenderer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{context}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{context}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 4. Initialize}
\PYG{n}{renderer}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{initialize\PYGZus{}shaders}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{renderer}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{initialize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 5. Render (in main loop)}
\PYG{n}{renderer}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Error Handling}
\label{\detokenize{api/renderer:error-handling}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PicoGL renderers include comprehensive error handling:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{OpenGL Context Errors}: Fallback to legacy rendering
\sphinxstylestrong{Shader Compilation Errors}: Use fallback shaders
\sphinxstylestrong{Texture Loading Errors}: Skip texture rendering
\sphinxstylestrong{Mesh Upload Errors}: Use immediate mode rendering

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{try}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{renderer}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{initialize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{except} \PYG{n}{OpenGLError} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{OpenGL error: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Fallback to legacy rendering}
\PYG{k}{except} \PYG{n+ne}{Exception} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Unexpected error: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Handle gracefully}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Performance Considerations}
\label{\detokenize{api/renderer:performance-considerations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modern Renderers} (ObjectRenderer, TextureRenderer):
* Best performance with modern OpenGL
* Requires OpenGL 3.3+ support
* Uses VAO/VBO for efficient rendering
* Supports advanced features

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Legacy Renderers} (LegacyGLMesh):
* Compatible with older OpenGL versions
* Uses immediate mode or legacy VBOs
* Good performance on older hardware
* Limited feature set

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Minimal Renderers} (Immediate mode):
* Maximum compatibility
* Uses glBegin/glEnd for rendering
* Lower performance but works everywhere
* No advanced features


\subsection{Best Practices}
\label{\detokenize{api/renderer:best-practices}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Choose the right renderer} for your target platform

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use MeshData.from\_raw()} for easy data creation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Initialize renderers once} and reuse them

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Handle errors gracefully} with fallbacks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Test on multiple platforms} for compatibility

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Choose renderer based on OpenGL support}
\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{has\PYGZus{}modern\PYGZus{}opengl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{renderer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{ObjectRenderer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{context}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{elif} \PYG{n}{has\PYGZus{}legacy\PYGZus{}opengl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{renderer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LegacyGLMesh}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{vertices}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{faces}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{colors}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use immediate mode fallback}
    \PYG{n}{renderer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{ImmediateModeRenderer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{vertices}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{colors}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets the layout for the rendering setup by binding the buffers and configuring the attributes.
The state is stored in the Vertex Array Object (VAO). This method assumes a single Vertex Buffer
Object (VBO) holds all position data but can be adapted as required. Handles optional usage of
Normal Buffer Object (NBO) and Element Buffer Object (EBO) if present.

\end{fulllineitems}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create VAO}
\PYG{n}{vao} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{VertexArrayObject}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add vertex buffer}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add color buffer}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add element buffer}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Draw}

\subsection{Performance Considerations}
\label{\detokenize{api/buffers:performance-considerations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modern Buffers (VAO/VBO)}:
* Best performance with modern OpenGL
* Efficient GPU memory usage
* Fast drawing operations
* Requires OpenGL 3.0+ support

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Legacy Buffers (VBO only)}:
* Compatible with older OpenGL versions
* Good performance on older hardware
* Uses client state management
* Limited feature set

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Immediate Mode}:
* Maximum compatibility
* Uses glBegin/glEnd for rendering
* Lower performance but works everywhere
* No buffer management


\subsection{Best Practices}
\label{\detokenize{api/buffers:best-practices}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use appropriate buffer type} for your target platform

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Upload data once} and reuse buffers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use VAOs} for modern OpenGL when possible

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Handle errors gracefully} with fallbacks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Clean up resources} when done

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{has\PYGZus{}modern\PYGZus{}opengl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

\PYG{k}{elif} \PYG{n}{has\PYGZus{}legacy\PYGZus{}opengl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ShaderType}} enum defines the available shader types in PicoGL.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Available Types}:
* \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BASIC}}: Basic color shader
* \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TEXTURE}}: Texture mapping shader
* \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LIGHTING}}: Lighting and shading shader
* \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NORMAL\_MAPPING}}: Normal mapping shader
* \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TRANSPARENT}}: Transparent rendering shader
* \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TEXT}}: Text rendering shader

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{picogl}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{shaders}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{type}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{ShaderType}

\subsection{Performance Considerations}
\label{\detokenize{api/shaders:performance-considerations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modern Shaders (OpenGL 3.3+)}:
* Best performance and features
* Full shader pipeline support
* Advanced uniform types
* Requires modern OpenGL

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Legacy Shaders (OpenGL 1.x/2.x)}:
* Compatible with older OpenGL versions
* Limited shader features
* Uses fixed function pipeline
* Good performance on older hardware

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Fallback Shaders}:
* Maximum compatibility
* Basic functionality only
* Uses immediate mode rendering
* Works on any OpenGL system


\subsection{Best Practices}
\label{\detokenize{api/shaders:best-practices}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use appropriate shader type} for your target platform

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Compile shaders once} and reuse them

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Handle compilation errors} gracefully

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use fallback shaders} for compatibility

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Test on multiple platforms} for compatibility

\end{enumerate}

    \PYG{n}{shader} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{ShaderProgram}\PYG{p}{(}

        \PYG{n}{fragment\PYGZus{}source\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{fragment.glsl}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{elif} \PYG{n}{has\PYGZus{}legacy\PYGZus{}opengl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

\subsection{Project Structure}
\label{\detokenize{development:project-structure}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PicoGL follows a modular architecture with clear separation of concerns:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
picogl/
├── backend/           \PYGZsh{} OpenGL backend implementations
│   ├── modern/        \PYGZsh{} Modern OpenGL 3.3+ backend
│   └── legacy/        \PYGZsh{} Legacy OpenGL 1.x/2.x backend
├── buffers/           \PYGZsh{} Buffer management
│   ├── vertex/        \PYGZsh{} Vertex buffer implementations
│   └── attributes/    \PYGZsh{} Attribute specifications
├── renderer/          \PYGZsh{} Core rendering classes
│   ├── meshdata.py    \PYGZsh{} Mesh data management
│   ├── object.py      \PYGZsh{} Object renderer
│   └── texture.py     \PYGZsh{} Texture renderer
├── shaders/           \PYGZsh{} Shader management
│   ├── compile.py     \PYGZsh{} Shader compilation
│   ├── load.py        \PYGZsh{} Shader loading
│   └── manager.py     \PYGZsh{} Shader manager
├── ui/                \PYGZsh{} User interface
│   └── backend/       \PYGZsh{} UI backends (GLUT, Qt)
├── utils/             \PYGZsh{} Utility functions
│   ├── loader/        \PYGZsh{} Data loaders
│   └── texture.py     \PYGZsh{} Texture utilities
└── tests/             \PYGZsh{} Unit tests
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Features}:
* Vertex Array Objects (VAOs)
* Modern shader pipeline
* Advanced uniform types
* Efficient buffer management

\sphinxAtStartPar

* \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VertexArrayObject}}: VAO management

\subsection{Release Process}
\label{\detokenize{development:release-process}}

\subsubsection{Version Numbering}
\label{\detokenize{development:version-numbering}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PicoGL uses semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{MAJOR}: Breaking changes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{MINOR}: New features (backward compatible)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PATCH}: Bug fixes (backward compatible)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples}:
* 1.0.0: Initial release
* 1.1.0: New features added
* 1.1.1: Bug fixes
* 2.0.0: Breaking changes

\label{\detokenize{development:release-steps}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Run full test suite} to ensure everything works

\sphinxstylestrong{Build documentation} and verify it’s correct

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Create release tag} on GitHub

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Build and upload} to PyPI

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Run tests

\subsection{Performance Considerations}
\label{\detokenize{development:performance-considerations}}

\subsubsection{Rendering Performance}
\label{\detokenize{development:rendering-performance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modern OpenGL}:
* Use VAOs for efficient rendering
* Minimize state changes
* Use instanced rendering for repeated objects
* Implement frustum culling

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Legacy OpenGL}:
* Use VBOs when available
* Minimize immediate mode calls
* Batch similar operations
* Use display lists for static geometry

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example}:
.. code\sphinxhyphen{}block:: python
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Efficient rendering
def render\_scene(self):
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Set up state once
glEnable(GL\_DEPTH\_TEST)
glEnable(GL\_CULL\_FACE)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Render all objects with same state
for obj in self.objects:
\begin{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{if obj.visible:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
obj.render()

\end{description}
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Clean up state
glDisable(GL\_CULL\_FACE)
glDisable(GL\_DEPTH\_TEST)
\end{quote}
\end{quote}


\subsubsection{Memory Management}
\label{\detokenize{development:memory-management}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Buffer Management}:
* Upload data once and reuse
* Delete unused buffers
* Use appropriate buffer types
* Monitor memory usage

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example}:
.. code\sphinxhyphen{}block:: python
\begin{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{class MeshManager:}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{def \_\_init\_\_(self):}
\sphinxAtStartPar
self.meshes = \{\}
self.buffers = \{\}

\sphinxlineitem{def load\_mesh(self, name, data):}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{if name not in self.meshes:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Create new mesh
mesh = self.create\_mesh(data)
self.meshes{[}name{]} = mesh
self.buffers{[}name{]} = mesh.get\_buffers()

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
return self.meshes{[}name{]}

\sphinxlineitem{def cleanup(self):}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{for buffers in self.buffers.values():}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{for buffer in buffers:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
buffer.delete()

\end{description}

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
self.buffers.clear()
self.meshes.clear()

\end{description}

\end{description}
\end{quote}

\subsection{Common Issues}
\label{\detokenize{development:common-issues}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{OpenGL Context Issues}:

* Check for context loss
* Handle context recreation

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Memory Issues}:
* Monitor buffer usage
* Clean up unused resources
* Use appropriate data types

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance Issues}:
* Profile rendering code
* Optimize draw calls
* Use appropriate rendering techniques

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}platform Issues}:
* Test on multiple platforms
* Handle platform\sphinxhyphen{}specific differences
* Use fallback implementations
